summary.plain: UA1's first sighting of the W boson: six electron events with energy that seemed to vanish, the signature of an invisible neutrino carrying it away.
summary.technical: UA1 Collaboration, Phys. Lett. B 122 (1983) 103-116; isolated high-transverse-energy electrons with missing transverse energy at sqrt(s)=540 GeV, interpreted as p-pbar -> W(+/-) + X, W -> e + nu, with the electron-neutrino system consistent with a particle of mass ~80 GeV/c^2. Announced at a CERN press conference on 25 January 1983.

title: Experimental Observation of Isolated Large Transverse Energy Electrons with Associated Missing Energy at sqrt(s)=540 GeV
why_it_matters: The first direct evidence for the W boson, the carrier of the weak nuclear force, confirming a central prediction of the electroweak theory that unifies electromagnetism and the weak interaction.
